Response A uses the older pre-.NET 11 workaround of manual `ReadToEndAsync()` coordination with `Task.WhenAll`, which, while functional, misses the purpose of the new APIs and fails to meet three of the four rubric criteria designed to reward modern .NET 11 patterns."

Process.StartAndForget is the proper, idiomatic way to launch a detached process and immediately obtain its ID without holding process resources, while Response A's approach of accessing .Id on a temporary object is less clean and relies on garbage collection. Both target net11.0 correctly, but on the core requirement—using the right API—Response B is unambiguously correct."
